title: Generative learning with Qopula circuits
journal_or_venue: 2024 16th International Conference on Communication Systems & NETworkS (COMSNETS)
abstract_summary: The paper studies quantum generative models (QGAN and QCBM) built on qopula circuits to learn copula distributions and capture multivariate dependencies in financial return data. It evaluates training strategies (regular, annealing, genetic), different continuous-to-discrete binning methods, and initial entangled states, comparing generated samples to a classical Student-t copula using KS and energy statistics. Results show QCBM (regular and annealing) can match or slightly outperform classical parametric modeling in these experiments and highlight factors affecting performance and prospects for quantum advantage on more complex dependencies.
methodology_description: The authors investigate quantum generative modelling of copula (multivariate) distributions for financial returns using qopula circuit ansatz. They convert continuous copula-space samples (probability integral transform of returns) into discrete target distributions by binning each variable into binary strings (concatenated per sample) using three binning strategies (generic equal-width, equal-frequency/endpoints, and k-means). Two classes of quantum generative models are trained to learn these discrete distributions: Quantum Circuit Born Machines (QCBM) and Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks (QGAN). The QGAN uses a variational quantum generator (qopula ansatz with RZ, RX, RZZ gates acting per-variable) and a quantum MPS-based discriminator. QCBMs are trained with gradient-free SPSA optimization (regular and an annealing-style curriculum where the cost uses a mixture pz(x)=µ pg+(1-µ) pr with µ ramp-down) and with a genetic algorithm variant (search on discretized angle grid, mutation/crossover and Euclidean-distance-based fitness). Models were trained for multiple circuit sizes (4, 6, 8 qubits total) and depths (4, 8, 16 layers). After training, samples from the trained circuits (projective measurements) are inverse-transformed back to continuous copula space and evaluated against the empirical/parametric baseline (Student-t copula) using two-sample goodness-of-fit metrics (Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic and energy distance/E-statistic). Multiple runs and bootstrap sampling were used to report ranges and confidence intervals.
algorithms_used: QGAN (Quantum Generative Adversarial Network) with MPS discriminator
frameworks: ndtest (Python package for KS and energy statistics)
experimental_setup: Experiments implemented with PennyLane (quantum simulation). Typical configuration: 6-qubit qopula circuit (3 qubits per variable) with 8 layers used in many experiments; other experiments vary qubits per variable (2–4 => total 4,6,8 qubits) and depth (4, 8, 16 layers). Models sampled 1000 measurement outcomes per evaluation; training runs repeated multiple times with different random initializations.
dataset_used: Daily closing prices of Indian stock market indices NIFTY 50, NIFTY BANK and NIFTY IT for the period 2014-04-29 to 2019-04-29. Log returns computed and then transformed into copula space using the probability integral transform (marginals mapped to uniform [0,1)).

experiment_input.source: NSE indices (NIFTY 50, NIFTY BANK, NIFTY IT) closing prices
experiment_input.preprocessing: Compute returns from closing prices; apply probability integral transform to map each marginal to uniform [0,1). For training/evaluation the continuous [0,1) values are discretized into 2^{n/m} bins per variable using three alternative binning schemes (generic equal-width, equal-count/endpoints, and k-means). Target discrete distributions created by concatenating per-variable binary encodings.
experiment_input.dataset_size_and_sampling: Original multi-year time series (dates above). For evaluation the authors bootstrap 1000-sample sets from the data; from each trained circuit they sample 1000 measurement outcomes per evaluation and repeat sampling sets for statistics.

experiment_process: 1) Prepare data: compute returns and probability-integral-transform to copula space. 2) Discretize continuous copula values into binary strings per variable using a chosen binning strategy (generic equal-width, equal-endpoint/equal-frequency, or k-means). 3) Construct target discrete distribution (histogram over 2^n basis states). 4) Define qopula generator ansatz (layers of RZ, RX, RZZ gates acting per-variable). For QGAN: use quantum generator + quantum MPS discriminator (generator outputs basis-state probabilities, loaded into discriminator, discriminator is MPS circuit). For QCBM: directly use generator as the Born machine. 5) Train models: QCBM and QGAN trained via SPSA (1000 epochs; SPSA hyperparameters a=0.1, c=0.1) using KL divergence as cost; an annealing variant trains on a mixture pz(x)=µ pg(x)+(1-µ) pr(x) with initial µ=0.8 and ramp-down schedule. Alternative non-gradient training uses a genetic algorithm (I=200 iterations, N=100 new candidates per iteration, M=25 elite for mutation, discretized angle grid K from [-π,π] split into 2^m points where m = total qubit count; mutation probability α decays multiplicatively by e^{-β} per iteration with β=0.013863; ν=1 mutation per layer). 6) After convergence, sample trained circuit (1000 samples), inverse-transform binary strings back to continuous copula values (by mapping bin endpoints and sampling uniformly within intervals) to obtain generated continuous samples. 7) Evaluate using two-sample KS statistic and energy distance (E-statistic) vs bootstrapped real samples; also compare to Student-t copula parametric model. Multiple independent runs performed (typically 5 runs for main experiments; for binning evaluation 20 runs).
experiment_output: Outputs are trained circuit parameters and sampled outputs (binary strings -> continuous copula samples). Evaluation metrics reported: Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) statistic and energy distance (E-statistic) between generated and real (bootstrapped) samples; p-values used with significance threshold 0.05. Baseline comparisons against classical Student-t copula fit to the data. Results reported as ranges over multiple runs and 95% confidence intervals. Tables report KS and E-statistic ranges for different models and binning strategies.

reproducibility_notes: The paper lists architectures, training strategies, hyperparameters (SPSA a,c, GA hyperparameters, circuit sizes/depths), and the dataset date range, but does not provide a code repository or explicit random seeds. PennyLane and ndtest were used, and the dataset (NSE index historical prices) is publicly accessible, so experiments are largely reproducible given the provided hyperparameters and ansatz figures; however, exact circuit definitions (full gate parameterization), seed values, and trainer scripts are not provided which limits out-of-the-box reproducibility.
key_findings: [supported] QCBM models (regular and annealing training) produced sample distributions comparable to, and in some runs slightly better than, a fitted classical Student-t copula on the tested NIFTY index data as measured by KS and energy statistics.
[supported] QGAN and QCBM trained with the genetic algorithm performed similarly to the classical parametric model (Student-t) on the used dataset.
[supported] Empirical KS-statistic and E-statistic ranges (over multiple runs) for models and classical baseline are reported (see performance_claims).

[supported] The QCBM genetic algorithm suffered convergence and stability issues when the search space (number of permissible angle values or circuit depth) grew large; tuning mutation strategy and search space size mattered empirically.

[supported] Increasing circuit size and depth generally improved model performance up to a point, but very large/deep circuits exhibited degraded performance consistent with training difficulties (e.g., barren plateaus / vanishing gradients).

[supported] The choice of initial maximally entangled state matters: for three-variable experiments the GHZ initial state yielded lower (better) minimum KL divergence than the three-qubit W state; the W state's reduced density is not maximally mixed which impedes satisfying uniform marginal requirement for copulas.

[supported] The continuous-to-discrete (binning) strategy affects results: for this dataset generic (uniform) and equal-frequency binning performed similarly and better than k-means binning (k-means was suboptimal here).

[supported] An annealing-style training schedule (mixing generated and target distributions during optimization) improved training stability/quality relative to direct optimization in these experiments.

[speculative] Qopula circuits have a theoretical guarantee (cited from prior work) that in the worst case they can give exponential complexity separations against classical computation, suggesting potential for classically intractable joint distribution learning.

[speculative] Quantum generative copula models may outperform classical parametric copulas on data with complex, nontrivial dependence structures (authors suggest potential where classical models fail).
[speculative] Financial applications such as derivative pricing and risk aggregation are promising future directions for qopula circuits, but not demonstrated here.
results_summary: This conference study implemented qopula-based quantum generative models (QCBM with regular, annealing, and genetic training, and a fully quantum QGAN) to learn copula distributions of returns from Indian market indices (NIFTY 50, NIFTY BANK, NIFTY IT). Using six-qubit (and other sizes) qopula circuits and several continuous-discrete binning schemes, the authors evaluated models with KS and energy-distance (E) statistics versus a classical Student-t copula baseline. Empirically, QCBM with regular and annealing training achieved comparable and in some cases slightly better goodness-of-fit metrics than the classical parametric model on this dataset; QGAN and the genetic QCBM performed similarly to the classical baseline but with larger variance and convergence challenges. The study also found that initial maximally entangled state choice, circuit size/depth, training schedule (annealing), and discretization strategy materially affected performance. The paper cites prior theoretical work claiming worst-case exponential classical hardness for qopula circuits and positions these circuits as promising for cases with more complex dependence where classical copulas may fail, but does not demonstrate a practical quantum advantage in these experiments.

quantum_advantage_detail: The paper cites prior theoretical results that qopula circuits can generate maximally entangled states and have a worst-case exponential separation from classical computation (a theoretical guarantee referenced from earlier work). However, the experiments in this paper do not demonstrate a practical quantum advantage on the tested financial datasets; instead they show parity or modest improvements for certain QCBM training strategies. The claim of advantage is therefore theoretical/speculative rather than empirically demonstrated here.
limitations: Quantum models (QGAN, QCBM-Genetic) perform similar to the classical Student-T copula on the tested dataset; only modest improvements seen for QCBM-regular and annealing.

key_ideas: #idea:quantum-advantage — QCBM (regular and annealing variants) matched or slightly outperformed a classical Student-t copula baseline on KS and energy-distance metrics in the reported experiments.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Demonstrates training and sampling for 4–8 qubit qopula circuits (depths 4–16) on a simulator, arguing potential for NISQ-era generative modelling of simple multivariate dependencies.

#idea:hybrid-approach — Uses classical optimizers (SPSA), genetic algorithms and classical preprocessing (binning/k-means) around quantum circuits (QCBM/QGAN with qopula ansatz and MPS discriminator), showing a practical hybrid workflow.
#limitation:simulation-only — All experiments run in PennyLane simulation; no experiments on noisy quantum hardware or with noise modelling are reported.
#limitation:qubit-count — Experiments are limited to small total qubit counts (4, 6, 8), restricting demonstrated expressivity and real-world applicability.

#limitation:data-encoding — Results are sensitive to the chosen continuous-to-discrete encoding (three binning strategies discussed); the cost and fidelity of encoding continuous copula data into binary basis states is a major factor.
#limitation:no-empirical-validation — Lack of runs on real QPUs and absence of noise/fault-tolerance analysis means reported small advantages may not hold under realistic hardware conditions.
